reviews.scope: Tangent values and undefined inputs underlying Arctan and solutions
reviews.reason: Arctan and the solution family k*pi both invert the tangent function. The student must already know tangent values and that inputs with cosine zero are excluded.

reviews.scope: Evaluating sums of arctangents through a tangent calculation
reviews.reason: The addition formula is one standard way to compute the tangent of an angle sum before choosing the branch. Branch selection itself does not need the formula.
reviews.counterexample: Sum arctangents through complex-number arguments, e.g. (2+i)(3+i)=5+5i, or with a right-triangle construction.

reviews.scope: Inversion of tangent on a restricted one-to-one branch
reviews.reason: General inverse-function ideas make branch restriction natural. Arctan, however, is defined directly as the unique angle in (-pi/2,pi/2), so affine-inverse skills are not needed.
reviews.counterexample: Learn Arctan directly as the unique principal angle with a given tangent, without the general bijection theory.

reviews.scope: Point-to-point distance used inside the minimum
reviews.reason: Line distance is defined as the minimum of |P-Q| over pairs of points. Without the meaning of the distance between two points, this minimum has no content.

reviews.scope: Coplanarity and skew-case checks in the criterion
reviews.reason: The criterion explicitly requires telling intersecting, parallel and skew lines apart. That separates zero distance from positive distance, and skew lines are nonparallel yet do not meet.

reviews.scope: Parallel-line formula as a special case of the definition
reviews.reason: The formula computes the separation only for planar parallel lines in matched form. The general minimum definition neither needs it nor is founded on it; they are associated, not ordered.
reviews.counterexample: Define and reason about minimum distance for intersecting or skew lines without ever using the formula.

reviews.scope: Recognizing the line determined by the two points
reviews.reason: Knowing that two points fix a line helps identify which line is contained. Plane containment is still a separate incidence axiom, not a consequence of line uniqueness.
reviews.counterexample: State and apply the axiom for a given line passing through two given points, without invoking uniqueness.

reviews.scope: Sibling incidence axioms of solid geometry
reviews.reason: Plane determination and plane intersection are parallel basic facts. Neither logically supports the line-containment axiom, so they belong together without a necessary learning order.
reviews.counterexample: Learn the containment axiom first; it uses no plane-determination or plane-intersection fact.

reviews.scope: Distinguishing containment from intersection and outside parallelism
reviews.reason: The second criterion contrasts containment with one-point intersection and parallelism, which is exactly the h115 classification. That classification helps substantially, though the cases can be defined directly by counting common points.
reviews.counterexample: Define each case by the number of common points (none, one, all) without the formal position classification.

reviews.scope: Plotting boundary lines, test points and regions
reviews.reason: Half-planes, test points and feasible regions are sets of ordered pairs in the coordinate plane. Plotting and reading coordinates is unavoidable for this representation.

reviews.scope: Treating Ax+By+C=0 as an inequality boundary
reviews.reason: The general form matches Ax+By+C>0 and handles vertical lines uniformly, which is convenient. Slope-intercept forms plus a separate vertical case also suffice.
reviews.counterexample: Rewrite each inequality as y>mx+b or x>c and graph it without the general form.

reviews.scope: Exact polygon vertices by intersecting boundary pairs
reviews.reason: Exact vertices come from solving pairs of boundary equations and then checking them against the other constraints. Choosing sides and recognizing redundancy can be done without exact intersections.
reviews.counterexample: Determine the feasible region and redundant constraints by test points and graphing, without computing vertices.

reviews.scope: Center, radius and circle points in the formula
reviews.reason: The formula |OX-r| and the radial nearest point refer directly to the center, the radius and points at distance r. The basic circle concepts are therefore indispensable.

reviews.scope: Synthetic proof of the bound |XP| >= |OX-r|
reviews.reason: Triangle side relations give a synthetic proof of the bound, with collinear equality cases handled separately. Other proofs avoid triangles entirely.
reviews.counterexample: Minimize |X-P|^2 with P=O+r(cos t, sin t) algebraically, or argue with vectors.

reviews.scope: Meaning of the multiplication operation in each product
reviews.reason: Every evaluation route, whether tables, algorithms or regrouping, computes the multiplication operation. Its meaning as repeated equal addition is the conceptual base of all of them.

reviews.scope: Recalling single-digit facts with factors 2 to 6
reviews.reason: Recalled table facts speed up local steps. The node explicitly allows any valid route, so repeated addition or a different grouping can avoid those specific facts.
reviews.counterexample: Compute 4*6 as 6+6+6+6, or regroup so that no 2 to 6 fact is needed.

reviews.scope: Recalling single-digit facts involving 7, 8 or 9
reviews.reason: A fact such as 5*8 appears only if the chosen route pairs those factors. Regrouping or repeated addition reaches the same exact value without it.

reviews.scope: Multidigit by one-digit written step within a route
reviews.reason: The column algorithm is one place-value route for intermediate products such as 16*6. Mental decomposition or regrouping into tens are equally valid.
reviews.counterexample: Compute 16*6 mentally as 10*6+6*6 = 96 without the written algorithm.

reviews.scope: Justifying changed factor order or grouping
reviews.reason: The criterion asks for commutativity and associativity only when order or grouping is changed. Multiplying left to right in the written order never invokes them.

reviews.scope: Evaluating products that include a factor equal to 0
reviews.reason: The node explicitly demands keeping factors equal to 0 and the zero rule. p075 supplies that 0 times any number is 0, which any route needs for such products. Trailing-zero shortcuts remain optional.

reviews.scope: Planar positions of cells moved by a paper fold
reviews.reason: A fold reflects the moved cells across the crease, which locates them. Stack order, push, pop and LIFO testing are independent of reflection.
reviews.counterexample: Simulate abstract push and pop stacks, or test LIFO output orders, with no geometric folding.
